source: review/stride/insider-threats.json (Matt Adams, Actions Speak Louder Than Tokens, CC BY 4.0) mapped onto the sgit register and review/stride/agent.json by the sgit-ai CLI agent, 2026-10-11; the first pass in research__threat-modeling-tools.md §1.1 confirmed against code during the dossier step
actor_added: A9, the agent holding the key (review/intent/actors.json, status proposed → to be added to the register §3 with this table as its evidence)
autonomy_level_assumed: L2–L3: agents commit and push unattended inside a scoped task; a human reads the result afterwards

mappings.sgit: the vault key, token and .pem are on disk at 0600 under .sg_vault/local; keys appear in argv and in `vault info` output
commits are signed by the clone's key; any read-key holder can mint a key that verifies, so attribution is per key file, not per person
no messaging or ticketing surface in the CLI
the CLI cannot see the agent's reasoning; nothing to model here
mappings.verdict: deployment (monitor the shape of reasoning), not CLI

mappings.sgit: the write key is a long-lived bearer secret with no binding to a clone, machine or time; a token likewise
mappings.verdict: lands on an existing row; PKI phase 2 (wrapped, scoped capabilities) is the answer

mappings.sgit: agents write 61 % of this repository's commits (coding.sgit.ai); a backdoor in sgit-ai itself is a supply-chain threat to every vault
mappings.verdict: review process of this repository, plus the CI gate added in step 3

mappings.sgit: three workflows, SHA-pinned actions, no PR trigger, no workflow-level permissions block
mappings.verdict: lands on an existing row; one new item (permissions block)

mappings.sgit: no database; the index and refs are the mutable state, and a write-key holder can alter them (rewind guard detects, nothing prevents)
container escape is the harness's problem; sgit runs as the user
sgit keeps no log to delete; the reflog is local and capped; the host sees sizes and timing only
mappings.verdict: partly N/A by model; the gap is that nothing attributes a commit to a task

mappings.sgit: a harmful commit among many legitimate ones carries the same clone signature
mappings.verdict: new model item; control is outside the CLI (session logging), with one cheap CLI aid: a task id in commit messages

mappings.sgit: unsigned commits are refused under signatures-required by sgit clients; other clients ignore the policy
sgit emits no telemetry, so there is nothing for the agent to suppress; reconstruction depends on the host's metadata and the clone's reflog
exfiltration over MCP is the harness's surface; sgit's own egress is the pinned server only (0.21.0)
mappings.verdict: lands on existing rows for the sgit egress; the rest is deployment

mappings.sgit: /proc reads are the harness's problem; the PBKDF2 cache keeps derived keys in process memory for the process lifetime (TM-R16), which is what such a read would find
a vault is the data; an agent with the read key reads all of it, forever
an agent that prints or reads a key puts it in its own transcript; sgit cannot stop that, only avoid inviting it
mappings.verdict: lands on an existing row; the skill rule (step 5) is the CLI-side control

mappings.sgit: data lands on a host outside the deployment: SGIT_DEFAULT_BASE_URL did this silently before 0.21.0; http:// servers remain allowed
CPU/memory exhaustion on the agent's own machine
no cloud API in the CLI
flooding the host with pushes or clones
mappings.verdict: host-side rate limiting; not a CLI control

mappings.sgit: deleting or corrupting repository content: the write key can delete everything on the host; locally, `pki delete ..` and unguarded destructive commands
mappings.verdict: lands on existing rows, plus one new finding (SE-001)

mappings.sgit: container escape
harvested credentials used beyond the task: one write key per vault is all-or-nothing
mappings.verdict: lands on an existing row (the 10/08 review's 'no per-writer authorisation')

mappings.sgit: CI steps with the pipeline's service account: no agent step runs in this repository's CI
no identity management in the CLI
reaching live systems from an environment believed isolated: the unit and security suites fail any non-loopback connection by construction
mappings.verdict: mitigated in the test harness; for a real session the pinned server is the only egress
